title: Deploy graceful prefetch throttling for mixed-context spikes
creator: Anika Patel
description: Several customers reported production regressions where a small fraction of long-context requests progressively suppressed short/low-token-rate requests in mixed workloads. Root cause traces point to aggressive prefetch handshakes + eviction hysteresis that let a small set of long-context flows monopolize admission windows and KV cache residency, creating sustained queue amplification and multi-minute short-request latency spikes. This ticket implements an adaptive, graceful throttling layer for prefetch/admission to restore short-request velocity without harming long-context throughput under normal conditions.
reproduction_steps: Deploy runtime-1.24 with continuous-batcher enabled and default prefetch handshake settings
Send synthetic mixed workload: 1 long-context request (context 32k tokens) per second and 20 short requests (context 128 tokens) per second, across 10 tenants
Observe scheduler admission windows: long requests prefetch large KV regions and cause eviction cascades; short requests see queue growth and 95p latency spikes exceeding SLO
Capture traces and scheduler metrics (admission_rate, kv_evictions/sec, batch_fill_rate, prefetch_rpc_laten)
investigation_summary: 2026-02-28: First customer escalation (CUST-1291) describing intermittent 95p latency spikes for small requests during traffic bursts
Instrumented prefetch handshake and admission counters; found prefetch loops that allocate admission tokens ahead of actual token consumption
KV cache eviction histograms showed correlated spikes directly after long-context admission bursts (eviction hysteresis too high)
Scheduler logs reveal admission reservoir not accounting for pending prefetch memory pressure, allowing long-context flows to reserve disproportionate inflight windows
root_cause: Prefetch handshake aggressively allocates admission slots based on predicted future sequence length instead of measured short-request velocity
Eviction hysteresis was tuned to favor cache locality for long-context sequences, unintentionally starving short requests under mixed load
No backpressure mechanism existed between prefetch and admission that could gracefully throttle prefetch when short-request tail latency rises
temporary_mitigation: Rolled back the most aggressive prefetch tuning on Hosted clusters (hotfix 1.24.1) to restore baseline admission fairness
Applied per-tenant short-request prioritization policy in ingress to protect latency-sensitive routes for affected customers
Added an emergency alert rule for kv_evictions/sec > 2000 AND short_request_95p > 500ms to trigger on-call investigation
proposed_fix: Introduce Graceful Prefetch Throttle (GPT): an adaptive token budget for prefetch admission that scales with short-request velocity and observed KV eviction rate

Algorithm: maintain short_request_velocity (S) and eviction_pressure (E). Prefetch token budget = base_prefetch * sigmoid(k1*(S_target - S) - k2*E). This ensures prefetch declines as S drops or E rises
Add admission hysteresis window clamp to prevent long sequences from preempting more than X% of concurrent admission tokens per tenant in steady state
Instrument and expose new telemetry: prefetch_token_budget, prefetch_throttle_ratio, eviction_pressure_score
Backward-compatible feature flag gpt.enabled=false for canary toggles per cluster (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)
Small safety net: if throttle reduces long-request throughput beyond Y% in a rolling 5m window, automatically relax throttle by delta to avoid regressing throughput SLAs
rollout_plan: Step 0 (canary): deploy gpt.enabled=true to 1% of runtime-hosted nodes in region us-west-2; monitor short_request_95p, kv_evictions/sec, long_request_throughput
Step 1 (gradual): if canary stable for 4h with short_request_95p improvement and <2% long_request_throughput degradation, increase to 10%
Step 2 (regional): expand to 50% region by region with 4h observation windows and automated rollback triggers
Step 3 (global): enable for Dedicated pools behind control plane opt-in and provide customers an escape hatch toggle in Console
Rollback triggers: short_request_95p increases >10% vs baseline, eviction_pressure_score increases >15% unexpectedly, or customer escalations >1 per hour
observability_changes: New Grafana dashboard: Scheduler > Prefetch Throttle (prefetch_token_budget, prefetch_throttle_ratio, short_request_velocity, eviction_pressure_score)
Add trace spans for prefetch.allocate_tokens and prefetch.apply_throttle to link high-level traces to admission decisions
SLO alerting update: create composite alert that combines prefetch_throttle_ratio > 0.8 for 5m AND short_request_95p > 300ms
Add structured logs for admission decisions with tenant, route, and token_budget fields (for post-incident replay)
test_plan: Unit tests for GPT algorithm: boundary conditions for S=0, S>>S_target, and high E values
Integration test: mixed-context synthetic load harness simulating 1:20 long:short ratio, validate short_request_95p reduces by >=50% compared to current master
Chaos test: random eviction bursts and tenant spikes to ensure no deadlock with prefetch throttle
Performance benchmark: ensure median token throughput for long sequences does not regress by more than 7% at 95% cluster utilization
customer_communications: Notified customers CUST-1291 and CUST-1304 of ongoing investigation and temporary mitigations on 2026-03-01
Drafted postmortem for affected customers summarizing root cause, mitigations, and planned fix (link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/infra/prefetch-throttle-postmortem)
Will provide Dedicated customers a rollout schedule and per-pool toggle in Console prior to their opt-in
notes: Coordinate with Platform on Dedicated pool opt-in UX for Console feature flag
Sequence rollout with runtime-1.24 patch window and ensure private/offline upgrades have a documented migration path
Follow-up: schedule a 2-week post-rollout validation to watch for regression windows during peak APAC traffic
